input: Need to pick up dry cleaning before Friday.
expected_behavior: Recover the single task as one bullet. Do not split it into multiple bullets or pad with invented related content to reach a higher count.
notes: Draft acceptance case for PROMPT_CONTRACT_VERSION=source-determined-bullets-v1 -- floor case, single supported idea. Has no prior passing baseline, so status is acceptance_gate, not regression_guard -- report_benchmark.py must not describe an initial pass/fail here as a 'regression.'

input: Call the dentist to reschedule, and separately, remember to water the plants while I'm away.
expected_behavior: Recover exactly two independent bullets -- one per supported idea -- without merging them into one or splitting either into extra bullets.
notes: Draft acceptance case -- two clearly separable ideas, tests neither merge nor split.

input: Three things: renew the car registration, email a coworker about the project timeline, and pick a paint color for the hallway.
expected_behavior: Recover exactly three bullets, one per stated item, in any order. No fourth bullet invented, no two items merged into one.
notes: Draft acceptance case -- mid-range count, explicitly enumerated by the note itself. Revised to remove a proper name (was 'Sam') per review feedback, reducing accidental overlap with other benchmark fixtures' cast of names.

input: So much going on: the roof needs inspecting, the car needs an oil change, I owe a friend a call back, the gutters are clogged, I still haven't filed the insurance claim, the dog needs a vet visit, I need to return a borrowed drill, and I never finished setting up the new router.
expected_behavior: Use no more than seven bullet lines even though eight distinct supported ideas are present -- the cap is a hard ceiling, not a suggestion. Do not merge two independent ideas into one bullet just to fit under the cap. All eight ideas must still be recoverable somewhere across the full output (narrative and action items combined), even though at most seven may appear as their own bullet line. Do not invent a ninth idea, and do not silently drop any of the eight without a trace anywhere in the output.
notes: Draft acceptance case -- ceiling case, 8 source ideas against the 7-line cap. Revised per review feedback: removed a proper name that collided with an existing protected probe (was 'Priya', already used in gold_v1.2.1_probes.jsonl probe 05); changed the rule from exact-7 to max-7 (the prior wording self-contradicted by saying 'at most seven' while requiring exactly seven); and replaced 'drop or combine if necessary' (self-contradicted the 'do not merge' instruction) with an explicit requirement that all eight ideas survive somewhere in the combined output even if not all get their own bullet line.

input: Call the insurance company about the claim before Friday. Don't let me forget -- I need to ring up the insurance company about that same claim.
expected_behavior: Recover exactly one task -- call the insurance company about the claim -- as one bullet and one action item, even though it is stated twice in different wording. Do not produce two bullets or two action items for what is one restated task; that would be padding via repetition, not two supported ideas. Do not add a second fact, qualifier, or emotional reaction beyond what the source states.
notes: Draft acceptance case -- tests 'never repeat content to reach a target count' specifically. Revised per review feedback: the prior version used two emotional statements with slightly different information (a factual worry vs. a stress reaction), making one-vs-two ideas genuinely debatable. Replaced with one literal, concrete task restated in different wording, removing that ambiguity, and added an explicit action_count_rule since the same restated-task risk applies to action_items, not just bullets.
